more_info.overview: Lutein colour is a plant-extracted carotenoid preparation that can also contain other carotenoids, plant oils, fats and waxes from the source material. It is used to add colour or restore colour lost during food manufacture. Extracted from edible plant material, including marigold flowers, using permitted solvents. The extract contains lutein together with related carotenoids. The specified extract is a dark liquid with yellow and brown colouring.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; unripened cheese excluding products falling in category 16.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.daily_intake: 1 mg/kg body weight/day for the assessed Tagetes erecta lutein preparation (EFSA, 2010).
more_info.origin: Extracted from edible plant material, including marigold flowers, using permitted solvents. The extract contains lutein together with related carotenoids.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The specified starting material is plant derived and compatible with vegetarian and vegan diets. The specification does not establish halal or kosher certification.
more_info.side_effects:
The assessment found no genotoxicity concern for the specified lutein preparation.
High food-use exposure estimates exceeded the limit in some groups; long-term and multigeneration data were incomplete.
